pr_title: Track Job completion through Pod finalizers and status
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Tracks Job completion without depending on Pods to not be removed. Instead, it keeps a finalizer on the Pods until they have been accounted into the status.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #28486
Fixes #99368

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

Builds on top of #98817 for API changes.
Implements kubernetes/enhancements#2307 with the update from kubernetes/enhancements#2585

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
Track Job completion through status and Pod finalizers, removing dependency on Pod tombstones.
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

```docs
- [KEP]: http://git.k8s.io/enhancements/keps/sig-apps/2307-job-tracking-wihout-lingering-pods
```

review_comments: add a comment that `List` returns an ordered slice.
Done
Can you add a case with a corrupted interval?
Done
can we change ClaimPods to update the pods in their state after patching instead of doing another iteration here to adding the finalizers?
I tried, but the changes in the manager were too many. Maybe I could revisit in a follow up.
is there a way to isolate this change so the existing logic is used if the feature is disabled? it's hard to reason about the safety of this change for existing jobs when the new feature is off
the way would be to revert all the changes and add alternate implementations. I could do that, but we will probably miss the code freeze deadline. I added a lot of coverage for this.

Previously this field was counting pod failures, which are mostly related to the user logic, now this is counting something more. The API describes the Failed status field as "The number of pods which reached phase Failed.", should we update the comment to say "the number of pods that didn't succeed"?

Added a comment on why I'm counting them as failures. This is also part of the KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-apps/2307-job-tracking-without-lingering-pods#deleted-pods

@smarterclayton should we change the field description as @ahg-g suggests?
ping @smarterclayton
I think we should be good on this front.
Ack
What will DeletePod return when deleting a pod with a finalizer?
the request returns 200 :)
it will set the deletion timestamp, right?
Yes, updated the method's comment.
add a comment that this will patch newly claimed pods with ownerRef and finalizers.
Done
error rather than info?

Not sure. This would only fail if some other controller overwrote the same field with garbage.

InfoS with an err field is recommended for known/acceptable errors.
sg
Nit: godoc explaining what total is.
Done
does this add or overwrite the whole list? is the interaction of adding/removing finalizers with other simultaneous finalizer addition/removal tested?
adds, due to the patchStrategy
so the list will end up with a mix of pods from the informer cache (and so could change underneath us) and cloned ones. Do you see a problem with that?

We don't really modify pods. This is just masking the apiserver-side addition of finalizers that happens on adoption. Since pod adoption is not the usual path, in most cases we wouldn't clone any pods.
So I argue that we are not introducing any instability that didn't already exist.

Although a safer approach would be to clone all the pods at this point as some kind of snapshot. @soltysh wdyt? Is it worth the extra memory?

As I'm thinking through it, I think I'm ok with the mixed list. The only problem will be when a cloned pod will get updated underneath us, but we'll eventually reconcile that status. I'm not sure if cloning the entire list is worth that cost. At least I'd go with this for starters and we can always re-visit.
sgtm
